mainTopic: מוקצה on שבת: rescuing a מת from a fire, moving lamps and using their oil, a metal candlestick, and a bed set aside for money
overview: The amud opens by finishing the case of a מת in a burning house. חכמים let a grieving person move the body, because otherwise he might put out the fire, and רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה בן לקיש. A ברייתא then shows that רבי שמעון permits leftover lamp oil, against the strict view in the משנה. A new משנה asks which lamps may be moved on שבת, and a ברייתא lays out the views of רבי יהודה, רבי מאיר, רבי שמעון, and רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון. אביי explains where רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון agrees with his father and where he differs. The גמרא then asks why a cup, bowl, or lantern may not be moved. מר זוטרא concludes that רבי שמעון permits only a small lamp the owner expects to go out, not a large vessel full of oil. רבי זירא's ruling about a metal candlestick is challenged and restated: one lit as שבת began is forbidden according to everyone, and one that was not lit is permitted according to everyone. Finally, רב rules that a bed set aside for money may not be moved, and רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges him from the משנה about a new lamp. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The reason for allowing a corpse to be moved: otherwise he will put out the fire
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the earlier reasoning. If we do not let the grieving person move the מת in an unusual way, he will come to extinguish the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you do not permit him to move it, he will come to put out the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation that started on the previous page. It explains why חכמים allowed a rabbinic leniency of moving a מת during a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person is panicked about his dead relative. If we forbid even the light, rabbinic-level act of moving the body, he may do something far worse and extinguish the fire, which is a Torah-level מלאכה. So חכמים permitted the smaller איסור in order to prevent the bigger one.

keyTerms.meaning: he will come to (do something forbidden)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic principle: חכמים sometimes allow an איסור דרבנן so that a person will not end up doing an איסור דאורייתא.

phrases.english: If you do not permit him (to move the corpse),
he will come to extinguish (the fire).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא שָׁרֵית לֵיהּ, אָתֵי לְכַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a line of reasoning that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving the מת is permitted so that the panicked person will not come to extinguish the fire.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן לקיש regarding a corpse
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of tradition, רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה בן לקיש on rescuing a מת from a fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן שילא said in the name of רב אסי, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the halacha is like רבי יהודה בן לקיש regarding a corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the question of moving a מת during a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is passed down through three links: רבי יהודה בן שילא, רב אסי, and רבי יוחנן. It closes the discussion of the מת by ruling like the view of רבי יהודה בן לקיש discussed just before.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the הלכה about saving a מת from a fire on שבת follows רבי יהודה בן לקיש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Sheila said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ בְּמֵת.
phrases.english: The halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda ben Lakish regarding a corpse.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ בְּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after the reasoning is complete.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical law on moving a מת from a fire follows רבי יהודה בן לקיש.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: dripping oil may not be used because it is not prepared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to a line of the משנה: oil that drips from a lamp on שבת may not be used, because it was not מוכן for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: (The משנה said:) We may not make use of it, because it is not among the things prepared (before שבת).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to begin discussing it. This is a setup for the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil that drips out of a lamp on שבת was set aside for burning, so it was not ready for other uses when שבת began. Something that was not ready at the start of שבת counts as מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: we benefit from or make use of
prepared and ready for use at the start of שבת

phrases.english: One may not make use of it (the dripping oil),
because it is not among what is prepared.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין נֵיאוֹתִין הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the topic of the מת to a new line in the משנה about oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil dripping from a lamp on שבת is forbidden because it was not מוכן.

steps.title: A ברייתא: leftover oil is forbidden, but רבי שמעון permits it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that oil left over in a lamp or bowl is forbidden. רבי שמעון disagrees and permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The leftover oil in the lamp and in the bowl is forbidden. And רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same topic. It shows that the משנה's ruling is actually a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anonymous view, the תנא קמא, treats leftover oil as מוקצה because it was set aside for the flame. רבי שמעון generally takes a very lenient approach to מוקצה, so once the flame goes out he allows the oil to be used.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה spoke about oil that dripped out of the lamp. The ברייתא speaks about oil left over in the lamp or bowl itself. The גמרא brings it to show that the משנה's strict view about lamp oil is not unanimous, since רבי שמעון disagrees.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught (in a baraita):
The leftover oil that is in the lamp or in the bowl is forbidden.
But Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מוֹתַר הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁבַּנֵּר וְשֶׁבַּקְּעָרָה אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא on the same topic as the משנה line just quoted, revealing a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids leftover lamp oil, and רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: New משנה: moving a new lamp versus an old lamp
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may move a new lamp but not an old, used one. רבי שמעון says every lamp may be moved except one that is burning on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may move a new lamp, but not an old one. רבי שמעון says: all lamps may be moved, except a lamp that is burning on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It presents a dispute over which lamps count as מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view holds that an old lamp is sooty and disgusting, so a person sets it aside from use and it becomes מוקצה. רבי שמעון does not accept that kind of מוקצה. He forbids only a lamp that is burning right now, out of concern that moving it might put it out.

keyTerms.meaning: one may move (carry an object around)

steps.whyThisMatters: This short dispute is a foundation for later discussion of מוקצה מחמת מיאוס, meaning something set aside because it is repulsive, and of רבי שמעון's lenient approach to מוקצה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: מְטַלְטְלִין נֵר חָדָשׁ אֲבָל לֹא יָשָׁן.
phrases.english: One may move a new lamp, but not an old one.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַנֵּרוֹת מִטַּלְטְלִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: All lamps may be moved,
except for a lamp that is burning on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְטַלְטְלִין נֵר חָדָשׁ אֲבָל לֹא יָשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא allows moving only a new lamp. רבי שמעון allows any lamp except one that is currently burning.

steps.title: The ברייתא names the opinions: רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reveals that the משנה's first view belongs to רבי יהודה. It adds a middle view from רבי מאיר: every lamp may be moved except one that was lit on this שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: One may move a new lamp but not an old one. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: all lamps may be moved, except a lamp that was lit on this שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה in more detail. It tells us who holds the first view and adds a new opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids an old lamp because it is disgusting. רבי מאיר does not care about disgust. He forbids only a lamp that was burning when שבת began, because it was set aside for a forbidden use for the whole day, even if it later goes out.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the difference between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון. רבי מאיר says 'lit on שבת,' so the lamp stays forbidden even after it goes out. רבי שמעון says 'burning on שבת,' so once it goes out it is permitted.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מְטַלְטְלִין נֵר חָדָשׁ אֲבָל לֹא יָשָׁן,
phrases.english: One may move a new lamp but not an old one;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַנֵּרוֹת מִטַּלְטְלִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: All lamps may be moved,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִן הַנֵּר שֶׁהִדְלִיקוּ בּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: except for a lamp that they lit on (this) Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְטַלְטְלִין נֵר חָדָשׁ אֲבָל לֹא יָשָׁן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה with a ברייתא that identifies its speakers and adds רבי מאיר's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה forbids moving an old lamp. רבי מאיר forbids only a lamp lit on this שבת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a lamp that went out may be moved, but not a cup, bowl, or lantern
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון forbids only a lamp that is currently burning, and allows it once it goes out. A cup, bowl, or lantern used as a lamp, however, may not be moved from its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: except a lamp that is burning on שבת. If it went out, it may be moved. But a cup, a bowl, and a lantern may not be moved from their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's view. It adds that a lamp may be moved after it goes out, and then gives an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון the only problem is a lamp that is burning now, so once it goes out the problem is gone. The ברייתא then forbids cups, bowls, and lanterns filled with oil and a wick, even after the flame goes out. The גמרא will soon ask why these are different and whose view this line is: עולא says it belongs to רבי יהודה (step 11), and מר זוטרא says it is רבי שמעון's own exception (step 13).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even רבי שמעון, the most lenient on מוקצה, has an exception. The גמרא will need to explain it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: חוּץ מִן הַנֵּר הַדּוֹלֵק בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Except for a lamp that is burning on Shabbat.
If it went out, one is permitted to move it.
But a cup, a bowl, and a lantern
one may not move them from their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: חוּץ מִן הַנֵּר הַדּוֹלֵק בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the third opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a lamp that went out may be moved, but a cup, bowl, or lantern used as a lamp may not be moved.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון: one may take oil even while the lamp is burning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון allows taking oil from a lamp that went out and from oil dripping off the lamp, even while the lamp is still burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון says: one may take oil from a lamp that went out and from the dripping oil, and even while the lamp is burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the most lenient view of all, from רבי שמעון's son. It is about using the oil itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His father רבי שמעון permits leftover oil after the flame goes out, as we saw in step 4. The son goes further and allows taking the dripping oil even while the lamp is still lit, so for him that oil is not מוקצה at all.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four levels of strictness. רבי יהודה forbids an old lamp because it is disgusting. רבי מאיר forbids a lamp that was lit on this שבת. רבי שמעון forbids only a lamp that is burning now. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון even allows taking dripping oil while the lamp burns.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
One may supply himself (with oil) from an extinguished lamp
and from the oil that drips (from the lamp),
and even while the lamp is burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִסְתַּפֵּק מִן הַנֵּר הַכָּבֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final and most lenient opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil from a lamp that went out, and oil dripping from a lamp even while it burns, may be used on שבת.

steps.title: Where the son agrees and disagrees with his father
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון agrees with his father that there is no מוקצה here. He disagrees by allowing the oil even while the lamp is still burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון agrees with his father on one point and disagrees on one point. He agrees that this is not מוקצה. He disagrees because his father holds: if the lamp went out, yes, it is allowed; if it did not go out, no. The son holds it is allowed even if it did not go out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי compares רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון's view from the last step with his father רבי שמעון's view from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both father and son agree that a lamp and its oil are not automatically מוקצה just because they were set aside for lighting. The difference is timing. רבי שמעון waits until the flame has gone out, while his son allows taking the dripping oil even while the flame is still burning.

keyTerms.meaning: An item set aside from use, which may not be moved on שבת

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon
holds like his father in one matter,
and disagrees with him in one matter.
He holds like his father in one matter —
that he does not hold of muktzeh.
And he disagrees with him in one matter —
for whereas his father holds:
if it went out — yes (permitted),
if it did not go out — no,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיהוּ סָבַר אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא כָּבָה.
phrases.english: he holds: even though it did not go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how step 8's ruling relates to step 7's ruling by רבי שמעון.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Father and son both reject מוקצה here. The son is more lenient: the oil is allowed even while the lamp is still burning.

steps.title: Why are a cup, bowl, and lantern different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of רבי שמעון's ברייתא and asks why these vessels may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But a cup, a bowl, and a lantern — one may not move them from their place.' What is different about these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last line of the ברייתא from step 7 and asks a question about it. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allows moving a lamp once it goes out. So why would a cup, bowl, or lantern used for light be forbidden? The question is which reasoning makes these vessels stricter than a regular lamp.

keyTerms.meaning: A lantern (a glass vessel used for light)

phrases.english: But a cup, a bowl, and a lantern
one may not move them from their place.
What is different about these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the end of the ברייתא from step 7, which was set aside during steps 8 and 9.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason these vessels are forbidden to move, when רבי שמעון permits a lamp.

steps.title: עולא: The last line follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the end of the ברייתא switches back to the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: In the last clause we have come back to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question. The forbidding line is not רבי שמעון's at all; it belongs to רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this answer there is nothing to explain within רבי שמעון's view. The strict line simply reflects רבי יהודה, who forbids used lighting vessels anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause (end of a teaching)

phrases.english: Ulla said:
In the latter clause we have come to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause forbidding a cup, bowl, and lantern reflects רבי יהודה's view, not רבי שמעון's.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: Then why the word 'but'?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges עולא: the word 'אבל' shows a contrast with רבי שמעון's leniency, which would make no sense if the line were רבי יהודה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objected: If so, what is the meaning of 'but'?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא attacks עולא's answer by pointing to one word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'But' means 'unlike what we just said.' רבי יהודה forbids even a regular lamp, so for him a bowl is no different, and there is nothing to contrast. The word only makes sense if the same speaker, רבי שמעון, is now making an exception to his own leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: But / however — a word that signals a contrast

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'אבל' as a meaningless connector. The whole challenge rests on the idea that 'but' signals an exception to the speaker's own rule.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra objected to it:
If so, what is the meaning of 'but'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's answer from step 11.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ מָר זוּטְרָא: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אֲבָל
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that the last clause belongs to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'אבל' marks a contrast with the earlier leniency. Since רבי יהודה forbids everything, the contrast only works if the speaker is רבי שמעון.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: רבי שמעון permits only a small lamp
steps.stepSummary: The clause is רבי שמעון's after all. He permits only a small lamp, whose oil the owner expects to use, and not large vessels full of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר זוטרא said: It really is רבי שמעון. When רבי שמעון permitted, it was for a small lamp, which the owner keeps in mind to use. But these vessels, which hold a lot of oil, are not permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא replaces עולא's answer with his own: the strict line is רבי שמעון's own exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a small lamp, a person expects it to go out during שבת, so he still plans to use its oil. That keeps it from being מוקצה. A cup, bowl, or lantern holds a lot of oil and will burn all שבת, so the person gives up on it completely. That is מוקצה even for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Which his mind is on (he still plans to use it)
They are large / hold a lot

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even רבי שמעון, the lenient view on מוקצה, does hold of מוקצה when a person has truly given up on an item for all of שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, Mar Zutra said:
Actually, it is Rabbi Shimon.
And when Rabbi Shimon permits —
it is with a small lamp that his mind is on,
but these, which are large — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to step 10, built to survive the challenge of step 12.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction within one opinion (small lamp versus large vessels)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The strict clause belongs to רבי יהודה (עולא).
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict clause is רבי שמעון's own. He permits only a small lamp that the owner expects to go out.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי שמעון permits oil in a bowl
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון permitting leftover oil in a bowl too, which seems to contradict מר זוטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: Leftover oil in a lamp or in a bowl is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר זוטרא by re-quoting the ברייתא from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא said רבי שמעון forbids a bowl because it holds a lot of oil. But in this ברייתא רבי שמעון treats a bowl the same as a lamp and permits both. So רבי שמעון does not seem to forbid bowls.

phrases.english: But was it not taught:
The leftover oil in a lamp and in a bowl is forbidden,
and Rabbi Shimon permits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges מר זוטרא's answer in step 13, using the ברייתא from step 4.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: מוֹתַר הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁבַּנֵּר וְשֶׁבַּקְּעָרָה
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that רבי שמעון forbids a bowl.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא shows רבי שמעון permitting the oil in a bowl just as in a lamp.

steps.title: Two kinds of bowls
steps.stepSummary: The permitted bowl is a small one like a lamp. The forbidden bowl is a large one like a cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a bowl that is like a lamp. Here, it is a bowl that is like a cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that the two ברייתות are talking about different sizes of bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, the bowl is small like a lamp and will go out soon, so רבי שמעון permits it. In our ברייתא, the bowl is large like a cup and will burn all שבת, so it is מוקצה. מר זוטרא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here — used to tell two cases apart

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, what matters is not the name of the vessel but whether the owner expects it to go out during שבת. Small means he still plans to use it, so it is permitted. Large means it is given up for the whole day, so it is מוקצה.

phrases.english: There, a bowl similar to a lamp,
here, a bowl similar to a cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 and confirms מר זוטרא's view.
steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם קְעָרָה דּוּמְיָא דְנֵר, הָכָא קְעָרָה דּוּמְיָא דְכוֹס
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (small bowl versus large bowl)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון permits every bowl, so he cannot forbid a bowl in our ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון permits only a small bowl like a lamp. A large bowl like a cup is מוקצה.

steps.title: רבי זירא rules on a lit metal candlestick according to each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says that a metal candlestick lit on שבת is forbidden according to the one who permits moving lamps (רבי שמעון), and permitted according to the one who forbids (רבי יהודה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: A metal candlestick that was lit on שבת is forbidden to move according to the one who permits moving a lamp. It is permitted according to the one who forbids moving a lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a surprising, flipped ruling about a large metal candlestick. According to the lenient opinion it is forbidden, and according to the strict opinion it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits only a small lamp, whose oil the owner expects to use up (Step 13). A big candlestick is like the large vessels, so even רבי שמעון forbids it. רבי יהודה forbids an ordinary lamp because it becomes disgusting (מוקצה מחמת מיאוס), but a metal candlestick does not become disgusting, so here he would permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: A large metal candlestick or lamp stand
According to the one who permits (here, רבי שמעון)
According to the one who forbids (here, רבי יהודה)

steps.confusionAlert: The rulings are reversed from what you would expect. The lenient opinion forbids this item, and the strict opinion permits it. That is because each opinion's reason for its view does not apply in the usual way to a big metal candlestick.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
A metal candlestick that was lit on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: It was burning when שבת began.

phrases.english: according to the one who permits — it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון: it is a large item, not a small lamp.

phrases.english: According to the one who forbids — it is permitted.
phrases.notes: That's רבי יהודה. He permits it here because metal doesn't become disgusting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: פָּמוֹט שֶׁהִדְלִיקוּ בּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the רבי יהודה / רבי שמעון dispute, as defined in Step 13, to a new object.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lit metal candlestick: forbidden according to רבי שמעון (it is large), permitted according to רבי יהודה (it is not disgusting).

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה does forbid a lit metal lamp
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי יהודה holds only מוקצה מחמת מיאוס. A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה forbidding a metal lamp that was lit on שבת, which is מוקצה מחמת איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי יהודה holds of מוקצה because something is disgusting, but does not hold of מוקצה because of a prohibition? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, all metal lamps may be moved, except a lamp that was lit on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second half of רבי זירא's ruling. רבי זירא assumed רבי יהודה would permit a metal candlestick, but a ברייתא shows רבי יהודה forbidding exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's ruling only works if רבי יהודה cares only about disgust (מיאוס). A metal lamp is not disgusting, yet רבי יהודה still forbids it once it has been lit on שבת. That means he also forbids things set aside because they were used for a forbidden act (מוקצה מחמת איסור), so the candlestick should be forbidden according to him too.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside from use because it is disgusting
Set aside because it was used for a forbidden act (the burning flame) when שבת began
Is that to say? (introduces a doubtful implication)

steps.confusionAlert: "Lit on שבת" does not mean someone lit it on שבת, which is forbidden. It means the lamp was burning during בין השמשות as שבת began. That is why it became set aside for the whole day.

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Yehuda —
holds of muktze due to disgust,
but does not hold of muktze due to prohibition?
But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
All metal lamps may be moved,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִן הַנֵּר שֶׁהִדְלִיקוּ בּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת!
phrases.english: except for the lamp that was lit on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: Metal is not disgusting, so the reason must be מוקצה מחמת איסור.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מוּקְצֶה מֵחֲמַת מִיאוּס אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי יהודה half of רבי זירא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that according to רבי יהודה a lit metal candlestick is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה forbidding a lit metal lamp even though it is not disgusting. So he holds of מוקצה מחמת איסור, and the candlestick should be forbidden according to him as well.

steps.title: רבי זירא's statement is restated: everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רבי זירא's ruling. A candlestick lit on שבת is forbidden according to everyone, and one that was not lit is permitted according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. רבי זירא said: A candlestick that was lit on שבת is forbidden according to everyone. One that was not lit is permitted according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first version of רבי זירא's words and replaces it with a corrected version. In the new version there is no disagreement at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once lit, the candlestick is forbidden according to רבי יהודה (מוקצה מחמת איסור) and according to רבי שמעון (it is a large item). When it was not lit, neither reason applies: it is not disgusting and was never used for a forbidden act. So everyone permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was stated, it was stated like this (a corrected version of a teaching)
According to everyone; all opinions agree

steps.whatToRemember: A metal candlestick that was burning as שבת began is forbidden according to everyone. One that was not burning is permitted according to everyone.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
Rabbi Zeira said:
A metal candlestick that was lit on Shabbat —
according to everyone it is forbidden.
If it was not lit —
according to everyone it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי אִיתְּמַר הָכִי אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by rewording רבי זירא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correction of the received version of the teaching (rewording the מימרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא said the opinions flip: רבי שמעון forbids and רבי יהודה permits.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no disagreement. Lit means forbidden according to all, and not lit means permitted according to all.

steps.title: רב: a bed designated for money may not be moved
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב that a bed someone designated for holding money may not be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A bed that someone set aside for money is forbidden to move.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב rules that once a bed is designated for money, it becomes מוקצה and may not be moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money is מוקצה, and the bed was set apart for holding it. According to רב, this designation alone makes the bed forbidden, even when no money is on it right now. That is the point the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: That he designated or set aside it

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A bed that one designated for money
is forbidden to move.
phrases.notes: Even when the money is not on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מִטָּה שֶׁיִּחֲדָהּ לְמָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new מוקצה topic: whether designation alone makes something forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Designating a bed for money makes it forbidden to move on שבת.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: a new lamp may be moved
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רב from our משנה, which allows moving a new lamp but not an old one. This suggests that designation alone does not create מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק raised an objection: One may move a new lamp, but not an old one!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes the משנה to attack רב's ruling. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new lamp was made and set aside for lighting, which is a forbidden use on שבת, yet the משנה allows moving it. Only an old lamp, actually used and dirty, is forbidden. So designation without use does not make an item מוקצה, which seems to contradict רב's ruling about the bed.

keyTerms.meaning: A new lamp that has never been lit
Old, meaning already used and dirty

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak raised an objection:
One may move a new lamp
phrases.notes: Even though it is designated for lighting.

phrases.english: but not an old one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that designation for a מוקצה use makes an item forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A new lamp is designated for a forbidden use, yet the משנה allows moving it. So designation alone should not make the bed forbidden.
